topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture and outlines the focus on the initiation and resolution of the inflammatory response.

topics.label: Pathogen recognition, PAMPs, and PRR properties
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how the innate immune system detects infection and tissue damage using germline-encoded pattern recognition receptors targeted against conserved microbial and cellular danger signals.

topics.label: Toll-like receptors and downstream signaling
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the diversity, ligand recognition, and spatially regulated intracellular signaling pathways of Toll-like receptors.

topics.label: Cytoplasmic receptors and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: They describe intracellular pattern recognition systems and the multi-protein assembly of the inflammasome that matures pro-inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Leukocyte recruitment, trafficking, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how sentinel cells initiate leukocyte extravasation into tissues, promote drainage into lymphatics, and can trigger severe systemic pathology when excessively activated.

topics.label: Inflammation resolution, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the mechanisms that shut down acute inflammation, how damaged tissue is repaired, and the pathological or adaptive chronic states that arise when resolution fails.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture session and previews the upcoming lecture on the complement system.
